name: passwd
description: Without an argument, changes your own password (the old one is asked for first). With sudo and a user name, the administrator can set another account’s password, lock it or make it expire. Typing shows nothing, not even asterisks: that is normal. Passwords are stored as hashes in /etc/shadow.

options.description: Locks the account: logging in with a password becomes impossible.
Forces the user to change their password at the next login.
Deletes the password (an account with no password: avoid).
Shows the password status (active, locked, dates).
Maximum number of days the password stays valid.

examples.explanation: Sets alice’s password (for example after useradd).
alice will have to choose a new password next time she logs in.
